title: Microbiome and plasma metabolomics data in the Wenzhou Parkinson's disease cohort
author: HAIJUN He
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0
description: Dataset of "PD plasma metabolomics" includes LC-MS metabolite analysis in the Wenzhou Parkinson's disease cohort consisted of 140 PD patients and 72 HC participants, who provided plasma samples for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolite analysis. Metabolite identification was performed using a multi-step workflow integrating MS-DIAL (version 4.70) with several curated spectral libraries. Raw LC–MS data were processed in MS-DIAL for peak detection, deconvolution, and retention-time alignment. Putative metabolite annotations were first assigned by matching experimental MS/MS spectra against the Public MS/MS (version 15) spectral library in MS-DIAL. To enhance annotation confidence, the resulting spectral matches were further cross-validated using external reference databases, including the MassBank of North America (MoNA) and HMDB.   Dataset of "PD Microbiome" includes the 16S rRNA PD cohort comprised 102 patients diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease (PD) and 84 healthy control (HC) participants. This cohort underwent fecal sample collection, followed by fecal DNA extraction and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. For the collection of fecal samples, each participant collected over 1g of fresh feces utilizing a disposable sterile fecal sampling kit, or over 1 mL of fresh fecal solution using a specialized fecal sampling tube with 5 mL of nucleic acid preservation solution. The samples were then transferred to a storage environment maintained at -80°C within two hours post-collection, in preparation for subsequent microbiota sequencing. According to the manufacturer's plan, fecal genomic DNA was extracted utilizing the cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) method in QIAGEN TIANamp DNA Stool Mini Kit (Cat# DP328, TIANGEN Biotech Co., Ltd., China). The concentration and purity of the extracted genomic DNA were assessed via 1% agarose gel electrophoresis. Based on these assessments, the DNA was diluted to a concentration of 1 ng/µL using sterile water. The hypervariable regions V3-V4 of the bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene were amplified through polymerase chain reaction (PCR) employing the primers 341F (CCTAYGGGRBGCASCAG) and 806R (GGACTACNNGGGTATCTAAT) (Novogene; Beijing, China). Each PCR reaction was conducted using 15 µL of Phusion® High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (New England Biolabs, Ipswich, MA, USA), which included 2 µM of each forward and reverse specific primer (341F and 806R), 10 ng of genomic DNA template, and 6 µL of H2O. The thermal cycling protocol consisted of an initial denaturation at 95°C for 1 minute, followed by 30 cycles of denaturation at 98°C for 10 seconds, annealing at 50°C for 30 seconds, and extension at 72°C for 30 seconds, with a final extension step at 72°C for 5 minutes. An equivalent volume of PCR products was mixed with 1X loading buffer containing SYBR Green and subsequently analyzed through electrophoresis on a 2% agarose gel. Subsequently, the PCR products were normalized to the same concentration and purified using the Qiagen Gel Extraction Kit (Qiagen, Germany). Sequencing libraries were prepared using the TruSeq® DNA PCR-Free Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina, USA) according to the manufacturer's instructions, incorporating index codes. Library quality was assessed with the Qubit@ 2.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Scientific) and Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 system. Finally, sequencing was performed on the Illumina NovaSeq6000 platform, producing 250 bp paired-end reads at Novogene (Beijing, China).
